source_policy: WHO Classification of Tumours 5th ed. (2019) Breast Tumours; CAP Cancer Protocols; primary literature. Internal research substrate only.

classification_records.morphology: Neoplastic epithelial proliferation confined to the ductal-lobular system by an intact myoepithelial layer and basement membrane; architectural patterns include comedo, cribriform, micropapillary, papillary, and solid.
defining_features: graded low/intermediate/high by nuclear grade ± necrosis
ihc_signature: myoepithelial markers retained at periphery: p63, calponin, SMMHC
classification_records.grading_system: Nuclear grade (low / intermediate / high) plus presence/absence of comedo necrosis
classification_records.clinical_note: Non-obligate precursor of invasive carcinoma; management hinges on grade, extent, and margin status.

classification_records.morphology: Dyscohesive proliferation of small, uniform cells filling and expanding acini; classic type distinguished from pleomorphic and florid variants.
classification_records.grading_system: Classic vs pleomorphic vs florid (variant designation, not a numeric grade)
classification_records.clinical_note: Risk indicator and non-obligate precursor; classic LCIS is not staged as pTis in AJCC 8th ed. Pleomorphic/florid variants behave more aggressively.

classification_records.entity: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (IBC-NST)
classification_records.morphology: The default category for invasive carcinoma lacking sufficient defining features of a special subtype; heterogeneous architecture and cytology. Formerly 'invasive ductal carcinoma, NOS'.
ihc_signature: ER/PR and HER2 assessed on every case
classification_records.grading_system: Nottingham combined histologic grade (tubule formation + nuclear pleomorphism + mitotic count), grade 1–3
classification_records.clinical_note: Most common invasive subtype. WHO5 folded several former 'special' patterns (oncocytic, lipid-rich, glycogen-rich, clear cell, sebaceous, pleomorphic, choriocarcinomatous, melanocytic, osteoclast-like giant cell) into IBC-NST.

classification_records.morphology: Single-file infiltration of discohesive cells, targetoid growth around ducts; classic, solid, alveolar, pleomorphic, and mixed variants.
classification_records.clinical_note: Distinct metastatic pattern (serosa, GI, ovary, bone); pleomorphic variant more aggressive. E-cadherin loss is characteristic but not required for diagnosis.

classification_records.morphology: Well-formed angulated tubules with open lumina, single epithelial cell layer, low-grade nuclei; >90% tubular pattern required.
ihc_signature: absent myoepithelial layer distinguishes from sclerosing adenosis
classification_records.clinical_note: Excellent prognosis; frequently associated with low-grade DCIS and columnar cell lesions.

classification_records.morphology: Invasive sieve-like (cribriform) islands resembling cribriform DCIS but infiltrative; low-grade nuclei.
classification_records.clinical_note: Favorable prognosis; may coexist with tubular carcinoma.

classification_records.morphology: Clusters of tumor cells floating in abundant extracellular mucin (>90% of tumor); type A (paucicellular) and type B (hypercellular/neuroendocrine) variants.
ihc_signature: type B may express neuroendocrine markers
classification_records.clinical_note: Favorable prognosis when pure; mixed mucinous tumors behave per the non-mucinous component.

classification_records.morphology: Cystic structures lined by tall columnar cells with abundant intracytoplasmic mucin, resembling pancreatobiliary/ovarian mucinous cystadenocarcinoma.
classification_records.clinical_note: New entity introduced in WHO5; rare.

classification_records.morphology: Morule-like clusters of cells without fibrovascular cores in clear stromal spaces; reversed (inside-out) polarity.
classification_records.clinical_note: High propensity for lymph node metastasis; the micropapillary pattern is prognostically adverse even as a minor component.

classification_records.morphology: Tumor cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli, defined by apocrine cytology in the majority of cells.
classification_records.clinical_note: Frequently falls in the triple-negative / AR+ (molecular apocrine) space.

classification_records.morphology: Carcinoma with differentiation toward squamous and/or mesenchymal (spindle, chondroid, osseous) elements; subtypes include low-grade adenosquamous, fibromatosis-like, spindle cell, squamous, and carcinoma with heterologous mesenchymal differentiation.
classification_records.clinical_note: Chemoresistant relative to other TNBC; keratin IHC panel often required to confirm epithelial origin in spindle-cell cases.

classification_records.morphology: Invasive carcinoma with papillary architecture and fibrovascular cores; distinguished from encapsulated and solid papillary carcinomas.
ihc_signature: myoepithelial markers absent at periphery in frankly invasive areas
classification_records.clinical_note: Part of the papillary-lesion family; classification depends on myoepithelial layer presence and invasion.

classification_records.morphology: Biphasic epithelial-myoepithelial tumor with cribriform, tubular, and solid patterns and pseudolumina containing basement-membrane material; classic, solid-basaloid, and high-grade-transformation variants.
classification_records.grading_system: Classic ACC low-grade behavior despite triple-negative phenotype
classification_records.clinical_note: Excellent prognosis in classic form despite TNBC immunophenotype; solid-basaloid and high-grade-transformed variants more aggressive.

classification_records.morphology: Solid, microcystic, and tubular architecture with abundant intracellular/extracellular eosinophilic secretory material.
classification_records.clinical_note: NTRK fusion makes it a candidate for TRK-inhibitor therapy in advanced disease; occurs in children and adults.

classification_records.entity: Tall cell carcinoma with reversed polarity (TCCRP)
classification_records.morphology: Tall columnar cells with reversed nuclear polarity arranged in solid and solid-papillary patterns.
molecular_signature: IDH2 R172 hotspot mutation (often with PIK3CA)
classification_records.clinical_note: New entity in WHO5; indolent. IDH2 hotspot is a useful confirmatory molecular feature.

classification_records.morphology: Cells with serous acinar differentiation and granular/zymogen-like cytoplasm.
classification_records.clinical_note: Part of the low-grade triple-negative family; rare.

classification_records.morphology: Salivary-gland-type tumor with mucinous, intermediate, and epidermoid cells.
classification_records.clinical_note: Rare; prognosis grade-dependent.

classification_records.morphology: Salivary-gland-type tumor with architectural diversity and uniform cytology.
classification_records.clinical_note: Very rare breast analogue of the salivary entity.

classification_records.morphology: Well-differentiated neoplasm with organoid/nested architecture and uniform cells showing neuroendocrine morphology.
classification_records.clinical_note: WHO5 groups breast NET and NEC under neuroendocrine neoplasms; substantial overlap with IBC-NST showing neuroendocrine differentiation.

classification_records.morphology: Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasm; small-cell or large-cell morphology.
classification_records.clinical_note: Aggressive; distinguish from metastatic small-cell carcinoma of other origin.

classification_records.morphology: Biphasic epithelial and myoepithelial proliferation with malignant transformation of one or both components.
ihc_signature: myoepithelial markers (p63, calponin, SMMHC) in myoepithelial component
classification_records.clinical_note: Rare; behavior depends on the malignant component.

classification_records.morphology: Biphasic fibroepithelial tumor with leaf-like stromal fronds and stromal hypercellularity; graded by stromal cellularity, atypia, mitoses, overgrowth, and margin.
ihc_signature: CD34 may be lost in malignant
molecular_signature: TERT-promoter, and additional drivers in malignant
classification_records.grading_system: Three-tier: benign / borderline / malignant (composite stromal criteria; WHO5 removed isolated well-differentiated liposarcomatous differentiation as a sole malignancy criterion)
classification_records.clinical_note: Management is surgical with attention to margins; classification distinct from the invasive-carcinoma axis.

who5_collapsed_into_IBC_NST: carcinoma with osteoclast-like stromal giant cells
medullary carcinoma / atypical medullary / carcinoma with medullary features (now 'IBC-NST with basal-like/medullary pattern and TILs')
notes: WHO5 recognizes ~19 invasive subtypes. Medullary group was removed as a distinct entity in WHO5 owing to poor interobserver reproducibility; described as IBC-NST with medullary pattern / prominent TILs. Verify each record against the WHO5 blue book and current CAP protocol before advancing to writing.
